column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard, writers' evidence: the seal stamped when the work is finished is the painter's, standing for his signature (HKMoA read at source; Q47 A15's own sources), so V2.2's her statement is a seal, not a sketch makes ink heard as signed; that turn is refuse for the report, this row stays as its recorded disanalogy, and 3d keeps the printed page and the plain line.

Tue 17 Nov: evidence under Q83-038's collector's seal (most seals on an old scroll are owners', one Freer leaf has ten and no artist seal); a holder's seal needs a gloss against the signed picture (row 1), a second image staged, so store only.

Tue 17 Nov: store, at most a reference in 3d: Hsiang's seals lost their worth to forgers because no catalogue stood behind them, so never tie it to case l.114 (overpromising; the card's own disanalogy), and the record co-sponsors could check is her broker's statement, held for her (Q72), never Table 1, the WInS portfolio scaled; a seal story staged in 3d is a second image.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report: a connoisseur's seal as a certificate of quality is endorsement, the signed sense, and the card's own disanalogy (judgement, not holdings) breaks the mapping; store as a recorded disanalogy beside row 3.
Tue 17 Nov: the same selective, judging seal as row 4 with Taipei colour; Christie's lot text, the count of 17 at the NPM unchecked; carries row 4's refusal.

Tue 17 Nov: store, writers' evidence behind Q79-004 (the land register, the stronger twin for 2.0): the Shiqu Baoji seal means entered in the record; never listed in Table 1, which is the WInS portfolio scaled, not her record (held for her, Q72), and a seal in 3d needs a gloss against the signed picture, a second image staged.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a record says held, not still held is CONCEIT section 2's ink holds because each Treasury is held to its date, already in the store; colour from a popular book excerpt.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard only: model figures are seen, never held restates V2.1 (every model result is pencil); an approving seal also leans to the signed sense, so never a turn.
Tue 17 Nov: store colour: a stamp can be cut off, so proof of holding is the broker's record (Q72, UCC 8-503), already the store's; NPM journal excerpt only.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: the most-inscribed scroll in Taipei is the copy is a vivid endorsement-is-not-ownership fact, but in 3c it would be a second image staged and its job is V2.1's owned already; a judge may know the story.
Tue 17 Nov: colour only, no investing job (the card says so).

Tue 17 Nov: store only: naming the owner before the work is done is a promise, the signed sense, and the 3f link fails because the first plan missed on one date (NUMBERS 8s), not by naming early; Keel's translation.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: say Yu argues (his own reconstruction), never a forger cut as fact; 3e's point that a figure travels with its conditions is plain already (on today's figures, if cash waiting earns nothing), and a cut scroll would be a second image staged.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, a writers' note: over-stamping as a forger's tell echoes Book 19 (no stacked safety clauses), but the mapping takes two steps to explain and serves no part.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: closed is not owned, and Sharpe's sealed boxes (Q57-037) already hold the closure idea.
Tue 17 Nov: colour only, no plan job.
Tue 17 Nov: residency colour only, a 1960 craft supply quoted second-hand; no plan job.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: stirring maps to rebalancing, and the plan is buy-and-hold in Perold and Sharpe's terms with no trade between its dated moves and only two reasons to change (IPS l.17).
Tue 17 Nov: guard only, beside V2.2's ban on ink is permanent: never say a seal never fades; permanence belongs to the Treasury held to its date; abstract only.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: the convention's reason is decay and waiting cash keeps every dollar (row 21), so only the timing carries, which is IPS l.13's own phrase restated (the report evaluates, never repeats); a stick ground to liquid also splits the defined ink in two and would be a second image staged.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q65-016 (waits of half a month to 10.5 months, $1,572 at forwards) and Q17-029; the figures match NUMBERS, now at l.1421 and l.1114, not the card's l.1403 and l.1096.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard for row 20: ground fresh is a convention a master broke on purpose, so never say ink is never stale; no plan job.
Tue 17 Nov: refuse, the card's kill stands: slow drying argues for a gradual 2031 move, against NUMBERS 8r (the move stays 1 January, one day).
Tue 17 Nov: residency colour only; the type counts conflict (2 million against more than 10 million), so never a number.
Tue 17 Nov: store colour: a page cannot print a character not yet cast is the rule in another image, a second image staged if used; the order of claims is said plainly in 3b.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: no dollar counted twice is a plain rule that needs no type case, and the idiom's printing origin is not checked here, so never say the phrase comes from printing; type is reused, a Treasury pays once.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, as the card says: matrix collides with the store's correlation matrix (Q10-002), and a fund swap is said as Table 3 row 4 says it.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c, the true craft fact behind round 6's verb (inked in January 2028, inked before the 2031 meetings): a Chinese colour print lays each colour in its own pass, the next once the last is dry; a fact or reference only, never the clamp staged as a second image; say Chinese colour woodblock (douban is row 30's small blocks) and never nothing moves between passes, since VT's value does.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the limit of a frame the report will not stage; IBTA's 15 days early is already Q3c's and Table 3's notice watch.
Tue 17 Nov: store colour: one block per colour area is cash-flow matching in another image (a second image staged); the Taipei link is the NPM's exhibition page.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, a contrast: kento are marks, and 3e's registration marks (Q47 A5) need no Japanese twin.

Tue 17 Nov: fact verified, mapping false: the rest of each payment stayed pencil until January 2028 (CONCEIT section 3; $2,287 left to the 2028 deposit), so never the ten were never pencil; an artist with no pencil stage also cuts against 3f's first plan rubbed out; at most an epigraph candidate for Caplet, the last mile credited to its writer (Chung 2018) unless he quotes Chen Uen.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the instrument follows the obligation is plain matching (US-dollar payments, US Treasuries); the preface is read second-hand.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, as the card says: trade words (halftone) that panel 3 marked down, no new job.

Tue 17 Nov: residency colour, at most one clause in 3f or a residency aside: Taiwan's national museum first showed comic art in 2018; never the award year (1991 against 1992), and a censor's stamp is never a turn.

Tue 17 Nov: keep the three meanings as writers' evidence (only held by could ever be ink; made by is signed); drop the 3d placement: the gloss it needs is a second image staged, which tonight's voice round says fails.
Tue 17 Nov: cut the map to one item, row 28 as the fact behind 3c's verb; Chen Uen's 2.0 mapping is false (row 32), and the seal placements in 3d read as signed or need a staged gloss.
